agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Rogers diffusion, application and peer diffusion, and bounded organizational timing

analytical_question: As of the 2026-11-01 test date, how far has LLM-based generative AI diffused generally and as human-reviewed coding assistance, among individual technology workers and comparable mid-sized software engineering organizations in an unspecified geography? Under the hypothetical Fast Follower posture and six-month planning horizon, what bounded evaluation timing is justified without assuming company-level adoption?
general_et_finding: The closed diffusion-v0.2 snapshot, prepared 2026-11-01, provides sector-specific signals, not a worldwide LLM adoption census. E1-C1 reports 90% current workplace AI use among surveyed technology professionals in its 2025 cross-section (individual current-use level, exact item n unavailable); E1-C2 reports 60% of surveyed AI users using AI about half the time or more when confronting tasks in a retrospective three-month window (individual recurring-use proxy, not daily telemetry). E4-C1 reports 75.9% task reliance among 2024 DORA respondents, with E4-C2 showing 74.9% AI reliance for coding among respondents whose responsibilities include writing code. These are substantive self-reported use signals beyond tool availability, but the questions encompass AI more broadly than LLMs; geography of the E1 respondents is worldwide without usable country weights, and the 2024 sample covers 104 countries. E2's rounded 76% repeats E4, not independent 2025 evidence. E3 adds bounded 2026 qualitative student practices, not prevalence. D1-D3 show availability, integrations and development ecosystems only. Awareness, access, experimentation, current use, recurring use, sustained authorized organizational deployment and industry penetration remain separate measurement levels: no transition rates, firm-level denominator, duration of organizational retention or representative 2026 LLM-only prevalence is reported. Rogers' innovators, early adopters, early majority, late majority and laggards are relative adopter-timing categories within a defined social system, not labels assigned using survey percentages alone. For the named social system of surveyed technology professionals, substantial reported use suggests diffusion beyond innovators-only experimentation, but selection, AI-tool wording, missing timing cohorts and nonrepresentative sampling preclude an exact category or measured S-curve. For global LLM users, software organizations and hospitals, the exact Rogers stage, saturation and diffusion forecast are unresolved. Both 2024 and 2025 prevalence observations merit refresh under the supplied twelve-month review policy; 2026 retrieval or student publication does not update those observation dates.
application_finding: Application: LLM-assisted code suggestions, explanation, test drafting and bounded refactoring with review before merge, distinct from autonomous engineering. E4-C2 supplies historical individual coding-task reliance in its conditional respondent subset, and E1 supports broad AI use by technical workers; neither isolates this exact LLM workflow. Comparable peers are mid-sized software firms and their engineering teams within an as-yet-unspecified geography. Their percentages of pilots, licensed seats, routine individual users or sustained authorized enterprise deployments are not reported; product integrations do not establish peer penetration. Five Rogers characteristics follow; factor directions are conditional interpretations, not measured effect sizes. Relative advantage: E2 offers observational analysis and measurement guidance, not a causal productivity estimate, and E3 describes verification concerns; direction mixed/uncertain because suggestions may shorten drafting but errors, security review and rework may offset gains; condition: measure quality-adjusted lead time, accepted changes, defects and reviewer effort against a local baseline; confidence low for net advantage. Compatibility: D2 issuer-described VS Code inline/chat integration and enterprise access suggest a potential accelerator alongside existing editor/review practices, while confidentiality, IP rules and repository-policy fit may inhibit; condition: approved data flows and actual IDE/toolchain fit; confidence moderate for described features, low for adoption effect. Complexity: D2 describes extension/version dependencies and E3 reports bounded student verification practices; direction mixed/inhibiting because prompting, secure setup, update maintenance, training and code validation add work despite accessible interfaces; condition: track onboarding time, update friction and review load in the actual team; confidence moderate for dependencies and low for local burden. Trialability: D2's described free sign-up and admin access plus the hypothetical company's ability to run a bounded evaluation may facilitate reversible experiments, but permission, licensing, data restrictions and setup effort can inhibit; condition: obtain security approval and establish pilot exit/rollback criteria; confidence moderate for issuer access descriptions and low for realized trial cost. Observability: E2 recommends measuring license allocation and daily active usage while cautioning those alone do not measure impact; direction uncertain/mixed because trustworthy quality-adjusted pilot results and comparable-peer accounts can spread credible lessons while demos and publicity cannot prove value; condition: record denominators, utilization, review effort and outcomes over repeated observation periods; confidence moderate for measurement guidance, low for peer impact. Mechanisms: documented issuer ecosystem/editor channels (D1/D2) may lower discovery/integration barriers, but D1/D2 share a corporate ecosystem and do not independently establish a network effect. Candidate change agents are an engineering enablement lead and security/governance owner; candidate opinion leaders are respected senior developers whose influence would need confirmation from team interviews, not named endorsements. Engineering forums and peer exchanges are plausible interpersonal channels, while enterprise administration, CI, testing and code review are complementary assets; no universal standard or measured peer contagion is established. Accelerators hypothesized: accessible IDE integration and credible internal champions. Inhibitors hypothesized: data-handling constraints, verification burden, trust, skill erosion, procurement and switching/update costs. E3 supplies qualitative student-context support for skill/verification concerns, not their company-wide incidence. D3's medical-model ecosystem has no direct coding-application diffusion implication and does not evidence hospital documentation adoption.
organization_specific_finding: The case is a hypothetical mid-sized software-products/services company with a user-specified Fast Follower posture. Existing repositories, code review, CI, finite training capacity and pilot ability are test assumptions; actual tool access, baseline, jurisdiction, budget, policy and engineering-team adoption are unknown. Fast Follower means intentionally learning from credible peers before standardization, not an automatic Rogers early-majority category; its eventual relative category depends on comparable firms' adoption dates and the firm's own verified start date. The observed technical-worker individual-use signals justify examining a controlled coding-assistance trial now but do not place the company above or below peers or prove it is currently a nonuser. Within a proposed six-month planning horizon, a reversible human-reviewed pilot can be considered after data-handling/security and owner approval, with bounded repositories, participants and tasks. Later standardization is conditional on repeated quality-adjusted results, authorized meaningful use, acceptable security/rework outcomes, and comparable-peer evidence; adverse findings or unapproved data flows would delay, narrow or stop the trial. No deployment authorization, industry ranking or precise Rogers stage is implied.

evidence.claim: E1-C1: 90% of surveyed technology professionals reported workplace AI use; individual current use, not LLM-only or enterprise penetration. E1-C2: 60% of surveyed AI users reported use about half the time or more on problems/tasks across the preceding three months; conditional frequency, not daily activity.
evidence.date_or_recency: Published 2025 (associated September 2025 release); 2025 survey, exact fieldwork dates not reported in supplied evidence; reviewed as of 2026-11-01; over twelve-month refresh threshold by policy.
evidence.evidence_type: Original issuer empirical cross-sectional self-report infographic and inspected questionnaire
evidence.notes: Nearly 5,000 technology professionals worldwide, exact item n, recruitment and weighting not reported in accessible 2025 materials. Broad AI-tool question, not specific LLMs; three-month self-recall is neither telemetry nor longitudinal retention. Vendor ecosystem affiliation; not a probability census. Publication date, survey period and source retrieval are distinct.

evidence.claim: E2-C1 repeats 2024 reliance (~76%, E4-C1 75.9%), not independent 2025 data. E2-C2 defines team-work incorporation as respondent-estimated percent of team work supported over three months. E2-C3 recommends licensing and daily-active-user telemetry but cautions against treating them as impact measures.
evidence.date_or_recency: March 2025 issuer-stated release, PDF v.2025.2; underlying 2024 survey and September 2024 interviews; not a new 2025 prevalence wave.
evidence.evidence_type: Publisher secondary analysis of original 2024 observational data, Bayesian modeling and qualitative interviews; measurement guidance
evidence.notes: Underlying near-3,000 respondent survey across 104 countries; 10 developers interviewed approximately 90 minutes each in September 2024. Team-work percentage is respondent perception, not company deployment. No randomized AI adoption treatment or causal productivity coefficient accepted. Shares E4 data; do not double-count.

evidence.claim: E3-C1: participants describe independent attempts, alternating assisted and unassisted work, verifying output and concerns about dependence or skill development; no prevalence claim.
evidence.date_or_recency: Published and updated 2026-02-17; eight-month project, exact fieldwork calendar dates not reported in supplied evidence.
evidence.evidence_type: Original author-reported university mixed-methods study, qualitative themes
evidence.notes: UC Berkeley EECS, design and data science students; sample size, sampling frame and response rate not stated. Suggests possible verification/skill mechanisms, not professional firm rates or causal effects. Repeated DORA statistics are not new samples.

evidence.claim: E4-C1: 75.9% of 2024 DORA item respondents report some AI reliance in professional responsibilities; E4-C2: 74.9% among respondents whose responsibilities include writing code report some AI reliance in coding tasks; E4-C3 describes recruitment and sample context.
evidence.date_or_recency: 2024 report, archived v.2024.3; 2024 annual survey, fieldwork start/end not reported in supplied evidence; historical as of 2026-11-01.
evidence.evidence_type: Original observational cross-sectional professional self-report survey and inspected original methods
evidence.notes: Nearly 3,000 working professionals across 104 countries; blog/email/social/snowball and supplementary-panel recruitment; three randomized questionnaire flows, not randomized AI treatment. Exact item n differs or unavailable. Self-selection and broader-AI definitions limit inference; conditional coder denominator must not be expanded to all firms.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: E1 and E4 demonstrate reported technical-worker use, but broad AI wording, nonprobability/unknown 2025 recruitment, missing item denominators and differing survey periods prevent LLM-only population prevalence, 2024-to-2025 growth calculations or an exact Rogers stage.
E2's ~76% is E4's 75.9% rounded and repeated. Three-month task frequency, team self-estimates and vendor access descriptions do not establish sustained, authorized company-wide production use.
E3's bounded student accounts of verification and dependency concerns counter a frictionless-use narrative but do not establish how common those barriers are in software companies.

No verified representative comparable-firm denominator, peer start dates, local telemetry, accepted-code quality results or counterfactual are supplied; missing evidence is not evidence that peers or this company have not adopted.

D3 and the technical-worker surveys cannot establish the claim that most comparable hospitals routinely use LLM-assisted clinical documentation. Inaccessible healthcare, Stack Overflow, METR and full DORA source leads contribute no findings; the available evidence cannot certify safety or causal productivity benefits.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence that source-reported AI use was substantial among the surveyed 2024-2025 technology workers, because original survey materials and 2024 methods were inspected; low confidence in extrapolation to 2026, LLM-only use, worldwide Rogers stage or firm-level penetration. Moderate confidence that coding-assistance product access/integration options were described in original vendor documents, but low confidence in current terms or realized use. Low confidence in precise application/peer diffusion and firm ranking due to absent representative comparable-firm and sustained deployment data. Low-to-moderate confidence in a bounded evaluation as a reasonable conditional timing option, relying explicitly on hypothetical CI/review capacity and unspecified geography, policy and baseline. Observation dates are older than the 12-month refresh flag; 2026 student findings are not a professional prevalence update. Factor directions and candidate mechanisms are hypotheses, not measured causal effects.
value_opportunity_implication: A reversible, human-reviewed coding-assistance evaluation could reveal whether suggestions, explanations, test drafts or bounded refactors reduce quality-adjusted cycle time while preserving maintainability, security and developer learning. E1/E4 suggest that some technical workers already use AI, making local examination worthwhile, but no general or local ROI, time-saved percentage or productivity uplift can be claimed. Compare genuine engineering outcomes and rework against a documented local baseline before considering standardization.
risk_governance_implication: Keep engineers accountable for generated code and require review and relevant testing before merge; passing tests alone does not prove security. Security and legal/policy owners must assess repository confidentiality, third-party data handling, IP/licensing, auditability, approved tool/model configuration and rollback capability before any pilot. Track incorrect/insecure suggestions, reviewer burden and skill-dependence concerns. The diffusion specialist neither certifies compliance nor authorizes deployment.
recommendation_management_implication: For the hypothetical Fast Follower, propose an immediate baseline-and-peer evidence audit led by engineering enablement and security, then seek accountable human approval for a restricted, reversible human-reviewed pilot if data handling and toolchain prerequisites are met. Define eligible developers, tasks, duration, meaningful weekly activity, repeated cohorts, review/rework and code-quality measures in advance; distinguish access, pilots and authorized routine use. At a proposed 6-8-week pilot review event within the assumed six-month horizon, compare results and obtain dated peer evidence before any broader standardization discussion. Delay, narrow or reverse if data controls cannot be approved, quality-adjusted results fail agreed local gates, security incidents appear or sustained use is absent. Thresholds and review dates are management proposals, not empirical values. Escalate the full adoption choice to the Adoption Agent and accountable decision makers.
change_monitoring_triggers: Engineering analytics owner: establish pre-pilot baseline, then separately measure eligible seats, access, first trials, meaningful weekly active engineers and repeated-cohort use with explicit denominators and authorized team scope; review proposed at weeks 6-8 and again before six-month planning close.

Engineering quality/CI owner: evaluate review time, rejected suggestions, test coverage where appropriate, escaped defects, security findings and quality-adjusted delivery performance against the agreed baseline; investigate deterioration and trigger pilot suspension under approved local gates.

Security/governance owner: confirm data-flow approval, approved repositories and configurations, privacy/IP restrictions, vendor/extension changes and rollback readiness before pilot and on material policy or product change.

Engineering operations and peer-research owner: obtain updated, dated, methodologically transparent comparable mid-sized firm evidence with geography, organizational/team denominators, explicit LLM coding workflow and sustained authorized-use definition; refresh historical E1/E4 signals rather than recycling them as current.

Accountable engineering sponsor: record management-approved success/stop thresholds and a formal reassessment event after the proposed 6-8-week evaluation; revisit sooner for material quality, safety or vendor-access changes.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Abstain from exact current global LLM penetration, diffusion S-curve, saturation, Rogers population stage or forecast date. Obtain a current original representative survey with sampling frame, dates, geography, tool-specific current/recurrent use, adopter timing and relevant weights.

Abstain from asserting most comparable software firms routinely or company-wide deploy LLM coding assistants, or ranking this hypothetical company against them. Require dated comparable-firm or engineering-team data with institution denominator, authorized production definition, workflow scope, repeated active-use cohorts, duration, retention and peer timing.

Abstain from the weak claim that most comparable hospitals now routinely use LLM-assisted clinical documentation. Require an original dated representative hospital/specialty survey or audited administrative dataset with geography, sampling frame, institution denominator, actual drafting/ambient documentation use definition, collection period and sustained use; technical-worker AI statistics and MedGemma access do not suffice.

Abstain from causal coding-productivity magnitude, net ROI and safety claims. Obtain local pre-specified quality-adjusted outcomes and appropriate comparison, error/rework/security measurements and accountable review; observational associations are insufficient.

Request this organization's geography, actual approved tool access and usage baseline, team/repository scope, code sensitivity, current policies, budget, pilot owner and planned reassessment date. These are unknown scenario inputs, not evidence of nonuse.
